sampling_model.design: One consecutive trajectory in the fixed common path space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) from a stationary regime \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\); identification is population-level and sampling uncertainty comes from temporal dependence.
sampling_model.units: Overlapping finite cylinders \(C_{\mathcal A}(S,a)\) on the fixed product alphabet, indexed by their terminal time.
sampling_model.treatment: A hypothetical intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x)\); no experimental assignments are observed.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cylinder assignment in the fixed product alphabet has positive probability, hence every denominator cylinder used by the returned expression is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Probabilities of the returned \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders are estimated by empirical frequencies and their long-run covariance by the modified-Bartlett Newey--West estimator with \(h_T\to\infty\) and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives sufficient summary-graph front-door conditions and a common do-free expression for selected micro total effects under latent confounding.
The ID algorithm returns an observational functional or a hedge and is complete for a fixed finite ADMG.
Theorem 1.1 bounds the graph segment needed to decide identification for one fully specified periodic latent-confounded time-series graph.
A possible-c-component and region recursion is sound and complete for causal identification over the finite graph class represented by a PAG.
Fixing kernels and intrinsic sets characterize identifiable effects and nested constraints in a fixed ADMG.
Do-calculus is sound and complete for macro total effects in latent-confounded summary causal graphs.
A complete graphical characterization and two finite adjustment sets identify linear direct effects from summary causal graphs under no hidden confounding.

Under causal sufficiency, the PMLR abstract describes necessary-and-sufficient graphical conditions for SCG total-effect identification and the paper supplies adjustment sets; the proceedings PDF states Theorem 2 as a sufficient-condition result.
Necessary and sufficient conditions and a pseudo-linear algorithm characterize identification by common adjustment in causally sufficient summary graphs.
Graphical fixing outputs can be compiled into weight-based and influence-function estimators under independent sampling.

body.tldr: SCG identification is already developed in several neighboring lanes: the PMLR abstract of Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui reports necessary-and-sufficient causally sufficient total-effect adjustment conditions, Ferreira and Assaad give complete linear direct-effect identification under causal sufficiency, Assaad gives a latent-confounded front-door sufficient result for selected micro total effects, and Ferreira and Assaad give do-calculus completeness for macro interventions under latent confounding. None of these results decides a nonparametric lag-specific micro total-effect distribution uniformly over positive semi-Markovian refinements with hidden confounding. Fix one finite alphabet family \(\mathcal A\) as a common input, so every compatible SCM induces its entire observed law on the same path space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). Because an SCG hides lags and instantaneous orderings that determine latent-projection districts, identification in each compatible refinement need not produce one causal functional of that common observed process law. The focal object is \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\), a finite offset-sensitive intrinsic-district transducer that returns either one arithmetic functional of finitely many \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders for \(P_M(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))\) over every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) or a bounded lag-switch hedge encoding two models in that same class with equal laws on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and unequal effects. The project derives an explicit termination radius, embeds Assaad's criterion in an explicit generic micro-SCG front-door family, maps every member of that family to a successful certificate, and gives a complete five-state trace for a lag-one identified query outside the family. It also reduces to ordinary ID on the static boundary and adds modified-Bartlett Newey--West delta-method inference for any returned functional. The bounded uniform fixing normal form remains the first-class open question; independent-shift lifting, an acyclic-summary reduction, and a positive stationary lag-switch collision are the supporting proof obligations and destructive tests.

project_justification.gap: The PMLR abstract of Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui reports necessary-and-sufficient singleton total-effect conditions for SCGs under causal sufficiency and the paper provides adjustment sets; Ferreira--Assaad completely characterize linear direct effects under the same no-hidden-confounding boundary. Assaad's hidden-confounded micro-total-effect theorem supplies one front-door sufficient formula but no generic front-door-class frontier or complete micro-effect decision rule, while Ferreira--Assaad prove completeness only for macro interventions on whole SCG clusters. Jahn--Karnik--Schulman bound ID after the periodic fine graph is known, Jaber and coauthors prove completeness for a fixed finite PAG, and Shpitser--Pearl give functional-or-hedge completeness for one fixed ADMG. None decides, for a fixed common finite alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), whether one nonparametric lag-specific micro total-effect functional is valid over every model in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) or returns two such models with equal entire laws on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) when refinement-specific functionals disagree.
project_justification.niche: Causally sufficient SCG total effects can be handled by adjustment, linear direct effects admit a separate complete characterization, and a defined family of latent-confounded front-door templates covers mediated configurations including Assaad's criterion. Macro do-calculus acts on entire temporal clusters and therefore does not answer an intervention on one coordinate at one lag. The remaining latent-confounded micro query requires district fixing across unknown temporal roles while holding the observed coordinate alphabets and product sample space fixed. Bounded lag and time homogeneity make these roles finitely describable, but quotienting time can destroy fixability, a PAG keeps a fixed finite vertex set, and a known-periodic-graph bound presupposes the fine graph. This leaves a distinct common-functional problem under simultaneous lag, ordering, and hidden-confounding uncertainty on one common observed-law domain.
project_justification.fill: The lag-robust intrinsic-district transducer takes \(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y\) and targets a nonparametric semi-Markovian lag-specific micro total-effect distribution rather than an adjustment estimand, a linear direct-effect coefficient, or a macro cluster effect. Its state carries offsets, fixing status, boundary districts, admissible instantaneous orders, and typed identities over cylinders of \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). An explicit generic front-door family is mapped member-by-member into successful transducer traces, contains Assaad's criterion as a proved instance, and is strictly contained by a concrete lag-one back-door success with a complete five-state trace. The normal-form theorem compiles one common finite-cylinder functional or extracts a finite temporal-role collision; independent shifts and exact-summary padding then convert the collision into positive stationary countermodels in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) with equal entire observed laws on that same product space.

body.related_work: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui (2024), Assumption 1 on p. 175, impose causal sufficiency and study the singleton total effect \(P(y_t\mid\operatorname{do}(x_{t-\gamma}))\). Their PMLR abstract describes necessary-and-sufficient SCG conditions and their paper supplies adjustment sets; Theorem 2 on pp. 184--185 is worded as a sufficient-condition theorem. In either formulation, the result is an adjustment theorem with no hidden common causes, not a fixing result for semi-Markovian latent confounding and not a certificate for disagreement across refinement-specific functionals. Ferreira and Assaad (2024), abstract and introduction on p. 1, give a complete characterization and two finite adjustment sets for linear direct effects under no hidden confounding. Their target is a linear direct-effect coefficient, not the present nonparametric lag-specific micro total-effect distribution. Yvernes, Devijver, and Gaussier (2025) give necessary-and-sufficient common-adjustment conditions under causal sufficiency; that output is an adjustment set rather than a general hidden-variable identifying functional. Assaad (2025), Lemmas 4.1--4.5 and Theorem 1, establishes a common front-door functional for selected micro total effects under latent confounding and sufficient SCG conditions. The explicit family \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}\) retains the front-door architecture through uniform path interception and two uniform back-door separations, contains Assaad's criterion as a proved certificate, and \(\mathrm{thm:frontdoor\text{-}frontier}\) proves that every member maps to TID-SCG success before giving a fully traced success outside the family. Ferreira and Assaad (2025), abstract and macro-query definitions, prove do-calculus soundness and completeness for interventions on whole SCG clusters under latent confounding. A macro intervention sets an entire time-series cluster and does not identify the effect of setting only \(X_{-\gamma}\). Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025), Theorem 1.1, Algorithm 2, and Section 4.1, bound the segment needed to apply ordinary ID to one fully specified periodic latent-confounded graph; the unknown refinement class and cross-refinement functional agreement are outside that input and output. Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2022) prove sound-and-complete conditional-effect identification for the Markov-equivalence class represented by one finite PAG. Their vertices are fixed and their output does not encode translation-invariant lag roles or strict-stationarity witnesses. Shpitser and Pearl (2008), Sections 3--4 and Appendix A, give the functional-or-hedge completeness theorem for one fixed finite ADMG; their hedges do not by themselves preserve time homogeneity, exact SCG summaries, and equality of an entire stationary process law. Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser (2023), Sections 2--4, provide fixing kernels, reachable graphs, and intrinsic sets for a fixed ADMG; these objects inform the state language but their invariance must be re-established under offset uncertainty. Yvernes and coauthors' abstraction hierarchy clarifies why graphwise success, a common proof, and common-functional identification differ. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022) inform compilation of fixed-graph functionals into estimators under independent sampling. Viviano and Bradic (2023) provide a beta-mixing inference lane for a different time-series target. Newey and West (1987), equation (5) and Theorems 1--2 on pp. 704--706, give the modified Bartlett weights, positive-semidefiniteness, and consistency under \(h_T\to\infty\) with \(h_T/T^{1/4}\to0\). Duarte and coauthors (2024) reduce discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs, but unrestricted polynomial elimination is excluded from the graph-native kernel. EasyRCA supplies the consumer and currently ranks adjustment-based direct effects under independent noises. All comparisons in the present uniform-identification claim hold \(\mathcal A\) fixed: model pairs are compared as laws on one \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and every returned cylinder functional has that same domain.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Strict stationarity and structural lag \(L\) do not imply a finite-order Markov observed law on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\); a lag-one shared-root process can have cylinder predictions that depend on arbitrarily long histories. The transducer may therefore use a bounded graph frontier and identities among \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders, but its proof cannot factor the observed process as an order-\(L\) transition kernel. Likewise, agreement of branch formulas on pairwise model intersections inside \(\mathcal P(\Omega_{\mathcal A})\) does not by itself produce one globally regular rational expression, so semantic gluing is not an admissible completion argument.
body.honest_scope: The bounded uniform fixing normal form, its lag-switch-hedge grammar, the explicit general state bound \(B_\star(n,L,\gamma)\), and arithmetic compilation on every positive common-law intersection are open. The independent-shift lift, acyclic-summary reduction, explicit lag-switch collision, generic front-door-family inclusion, Assaad-criterion embedding, and the five-state outside-family trace are supplied as to-prove statements, not presumed facts. Passing the front-door, outside-family trace, offset-sensitive fixing, and lag-switch tests for \(|V|\le3\) and \(L=1\) is necessary but not a completeness proof. The statistical theorem is conditional on a successful finite-cylinder output, geometric beta mixing, the Newey--West modified-Bartlett weights, \(h_T\to\infty\), and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\); it does not rescue an unidentified query. The finite family \(\mathcal A\) is fixed before the model class is formed and may be nonbinary; every compared model and returned functional lives on the same \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). Ranking across anomalous regimes would require separate stability assumptions not made here. When \(L=0\), the proposal reduces to ordinary fixed-ADMG ID.
